question: A man standing on the banks of a river observes that the angle subtended by a tree on the opposite bank is 60°. He walks 36 meters backward on the bank and observes the angle to be 30°. What is the breadth of the river?
solution:
**Given:**

Angle subtended by the tree on the opposite bank = 60° 

Angle subtended by the tree 36 m backward from the bank = 30° 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6256938f1ccfab15493fd932cec143058fdf05aaf25c3119589474dba35c7542.png] 

Let the height of the treee be = h 

Let the breadth of the river be = a 

In triangle BCD, CD/BC = tan 60° 

⇒ h/a = √3
